     Tables read the 05/06/07 analysis parquets + the evidence spans. Action

```{r setup}
library(arrow); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(readr)
library(stringr); library(scales); library(gt); library(here); library(glue); library(jsonlite)
options(arrow.skip_nul = TRUE)

ANALYSIS <- here("phase2", "data", "analysis", "deliverable06")
OUTPUT   <- here("phase2", "output", "deliverable06")
FIGS     <- file.path(OUTPUT, "figures")

verdicts <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "candidate_verdicts.parquet"))
mit      <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "candidate_mitigation_summary.parquet"))
clusters <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "ce_clusters.parquet"))
ce_land  <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "ce_landscape_ces.parquet"))
corp     <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "candidate_corpus.parquet"))
facts    <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "candidate_facts.parquet"))
inv      <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "fonsi_project_inventory.parquet"))
enr      <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "fonsi_enrichment.parquet")) |>
  filter(!is.na(action_summary)) |> mutate(is_mit = is_mitigated_fonsi %in% TRUE)
n_mit_dep_case <- sum(enr$is_mit & enr$mitigation_dependence == "case_specific_dependent", na.rm = TRUE)
n_mit_noncand  <- sum(enr$is_mit & !(as.character(enr$project_id) %in%
                                     as.character(filter(corp, is_fonsi)$project_id)))

# "bounded" / CE-shaped = the Rule-B flag from 09 (LLM-bounded + transmission shape gate).
# candidate_facts is now the candidate set itself (one row per FONSI, keyed on corrected action_category).
facts <- facts |> mutate(is_bounded = is_ce_shaped %in% TRUE, project_id = as.character(project_id))
corp_fonsi <- facts
n_clean     <- corp_fonsi |> distinct(project_id) |> nrow()   # analyzed clean-energy corpus (= candidate_facts); 1 inventory FONSI is dropped upstream (no evidence)
n_candidate <- corp_fonsi |> distinct(project_id) |> nrow()
n_ce_shaped <- corp_fonsi |> filter(is_bounded) |> distinct(project_id) |> nrow()
n_other     <- n_clean - n_candidate

n_new   <- sum(verdicts$verdict == "new")
n_adopt <- sum(verdicts$verdict == "adopt")
n_ce    <- nrow(ce_land)
n_units <- n_distinct(ce_land$agency_unit)
n_units_dept <- n_distinct(str_trim(str_extract(ce_land$agency_unit, "^[^-]+")))
n_xdup  <- sum(ce_land$xagency_near_duplicate, na.rm = TRUE)
n_xclust <- sum(clusters$n_agencies >= 2)
n_bounds <- sum(ce_land$states_any_bound, na.rm = TRUE)
# denominators + grain (scope table)
n_profile_rows  <- facts |> distinct(project_id) |> nrow()           # all corrected candidate FONSIs
n_llm_bounded   <- facts |> filter(is_bounded_low_impact == TRUE) |> nrow()   # LLM-bounded (pre shape gate)
n_enriched      <- sum(nchar(dplyr::coalesce(enr$action_summary, "")) > 0)
n_excluded_noev <- nrow(enr) - n_enriched
ce_snapshot     <- as.character(sort(unique(ce_land$source_version_date)))[1]
# candidate_category IS the corrected action_category now (set in 09), so rule-vs-LLM mismatch is 0 by construction
n_cat_mismatch  <- facts |> filter(candidate_category != action_category) |> nrow()
tx_mit  <- mit$mitigated_share[mit$candidate_category == "Transmission__upgrade"]
tx_mit  <- if (length(tx_mit)) tx_mit[1] else NA_real_
# --- refactor: tech_group x action grid verdict tallies ---
n_expand    <- sum(verdicts$verdict == "expand")
n_covered   <- sum(verdicts$verdict == "already_covered")
n_cells     <- nrow(verdicts)
n_dev_codif <- sum(verdicts$verdict == "new" & verdicts$is_codifiable)
dev_short   <- verdicts |> filter(verdict == "new", is_codifiable, n_profile_fonsi >= 5) |>
  arrange(desc(n_profile_fonsi))
n_dev_short <- nrow(dev_short)
n_tx_up     <- verdicts$n_profile_fonsi[verdicts$candidate_category == "Transmission__upgrade"]
n_tx_up     <- if (length(n_tx_up)) n_tx_up[1] else 0L
# FONSIs whose LLM action verb is "other" (the un-named-action frontier for net-new discovery)
n_action_other <- facts |> mutate(.act = sub("^.*__", "", candidate_category)) |>
  filter(.act == "other") |> distinct(project_id) |> nrow()
# adopt cells with substantive evidence (>= 2 CE-shaped FONSIs) — the rows shown in the adopt table
n_adopt_sub <- sum(verdicts$verdict == "adopt" & verdicts$n_profile_fonsi >= 2)

cstats        <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "corpus_mitigation_stats.parquet"))
n_mit_corpus  <- cstats$n_mitigated_fonsi[1]
mit_share_cor <- cstats$mitigated_share[1]
n_enf_only    <- cstats$n_case_specific_dependent[1]
```

## Executive Summary

::: {.callout-note}
## Key Findings

- **A data-driven grid of `r n_cells` technology × action cells** — every clean-energy
  FONSI placed by its technology (from D3) and its LLM-labeled action verb — resolves to
  `r n_adopt` adopt · `r n_expand` expand · `r n_new` develop candidate cells (plus
  `r n_covered` already covered; all pending CE-coverage verification). No category is
  hand-picked: the verdicts fall out of the grid.
- **Expand is the single strongest lever — transmission upgrades within existing
  right-of-way:** `r n_tx_up` bounded, low-impact FONSIs across 12 states (BLM, DOE, and
  the power-marketing administrations) match a transmission CE (TVA's #17 / #19), but a
  subset of long rebuilds exceeds its ~25-mile cap — so the move is to expand that CE,
  not adopt it as-is.
- **Most decarbonization FONSIs lean on committed mitigation** — `r n_mit_corpus` of
  `r n_clean` (`r percent(mit_share_cor, 1)`) are *mitigated* FONSIs, so a CE built
  from them must encode the recurring mitigations as design criteria, not rely
  on case-by-case commitments.
- **Adopting a peer agency's CE is well-precedented:** of `r comma(n_ce)` existing
  federal CEs, `r n_xclust` action-families are already shared across two or more
  agencies.
- **Net-new CEs are visible in the grid itself** — `r n_dev_codif` codifiable *develop*
  cells recur with no close existing CE (demonstration / pilot facilities are the
  cross-cutting standout). A further frontier is the `r n_action_other` FONSIs whose action
  the model could only label *"other"* — a recommended clustering next step.
:::

This report delivers:

> Technical support for new regulatory categorical exclusion development:
> identifying patterns in FONSIs.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Methodology

The deliverable runs **three analyses, each on a different data source.** They are
not a single funnel — only Analysis 1 starts from the full FONSI corpus; Analysis
2 works from the mitigated subset of it, and Analysis 3 works from the existing
federal CE catalog (not FONSIs at all).

| Analysis | Data source | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Scaling CEs (develop, expand, or adopt)** | Decarb EAs with FONSIs | `r n_ce_shaped`/`r n_clean` projects (~`r percent(n_ce_shaped / n_clean, 1)`) |
| **2. Mitigated FONSIs** | Decarb Mitigated FONSIs | `r n_mit_corpus` of `r n_clean` projects (`r percent(mit_share_cor, 1)`) |
| **3. Current federal CE catalog** | Existing federal CE catalog | `r comma(n_ce)` CEs |

Each analysis's scope is summarized above; its step-by-step Methodology (the callout at the
top of each analysis) and its own caveats appear with that analysis, below.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Analysis 1 — Scaling Categorical Exclusions (CEs)

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Methodology

1. **Data —** the `r n_clean` decarbonization EA→FONSI projects. A FONSI concludes a full Environmental Assessment, so each is a documented federal "no significant impact" determination — the evidence base for a CE.
2. **Label** each FONSI's action verb (new-build, upgrade, exploration, demonstration…) with an LLM, and pair it with the FONSI's Deliverable-3 technology — together these place it on the technology × action grid.
3. **Keep the bounded, low-impact subset** within each type — the small, routine projects that could plausibly be a CE (in-corridor upgrades, not major rebuilds). This is a yes/no judgment about scale, not a numeric threshold: a FONSI is kept whether or not it states an acreage or length.
4. **Match** each candidate against the existing federal CE catalog by text similarity.
5. **Compare sizes** — read the matched CE's stated size limit (acres, miles, kV, MW, wells), where it has one, against the bounded FONSIs' own sizes, to test whether ours *exceed* it. This is the only step where stated numbers matter.
6. **Classify** as develop (no existing CE covers it), expand (our FONSIs exceed the CE's stated limit), or adopt (a CE exists, but at a different agency than the ones doing these FONSIs).
:::

> This analysis asks how to scale Categorical Exclusions (CEs): where an agency could
> **adopt** a CE another agency already holds, **expand** an existing CE whose bound is too
> tight, or **develop** a new CE for a recurring action that no CE yet covers. It answers this
> exhaustively — every clean-energy FONSI is placed on a technology × action grid, and
> each cell is read as one of those three verdicts.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**The bottom line — three levers, read across every clean-energy technology:**

- **Expand — the strongest single opportunity.** *Transmission upgrades*: 26 in-corridor
  rebuild / reconductor FONSIs across 12 states still run as full EAs though a CE exists — its size
  bound is simply too tight. Widen it.
- **Adopt — broad but thin.** 22 technology × action cells already have a matching CE at another
  agency to adopt, but most rest on only 2–4 FONSIs — there is no single dominant case.
- **Develop — the genuinely new gap.** 16 recurring actions have no close existing CE
  (14 codifiable; 2 set aside as non-codifiable). The clearest is cross-cutting:
  demonstration / pilot facilities recur as a gap for wind, nuclear, and other
  clean-energy projects — the strongest candidate for a brand-new CE. *(Develop verdicts are
  candidates pending eCFR review; non-codifiable actions such as battery manufacturing are set aside.)*
:::

## The coverage map

Every decarbonization FONSI is categorized by its technology (an independent Deliverable-3
classification) and its action (an LLM-assigned verb), filling a grid of `r n_cells`
technology × action cells. Each cell is matched against the existing federal CE catalog and read as
adopt, expand, or develop. The coverage map below is the answer, up front; the three
stages that follow show how every cell earned its color — **build the grid**, **resolve each cell**,
then **rank the opportunities**:

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-coverage-grid
#| fig-cap: "The clean-energy CE coverage map — every FONSI by technology × action. Color = verdict (adopt / expand / develop / already-covered); a *develop* cell is a recurring action with no existing CE. *develop-excluded* = non-codifiable (manufacturing / land authorization). Number = CE-shaped FONSIs in the cell."
#| out-width: 100%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_coverage_grid.png"))
```

The `r n_ce_shaped` CE-shaped FONSIs — the small, routine cases within these cells — are the
actionable evidence carried through the rest of this analysis.

## Build the grid: label the action, keep the CE-shaped subset

A dedicated LLM pass labels each FONSI's action verb — new-build, upgrade,
maintenance, exploration, demonstration, and so on — which, paired with its technology, is what
places it in a grid cell. Within each technology we then keep the CE-shaped subset:

- **Bounded, low-impact** (teal) — the small, routine version that could plausibly be
  a CE: in-corridor work, short segments, previously disturbed land, no major new
  construction. *These are what we carry forward.*
- **Broader** (grey) — the larger or greenfield projects (major rebuilds, new
  corridors, utility-scale greenfield). Set aside; not CE-shaped.

```{r}
#| echo: false
.prof <- facts |> filter(is_profile_subtype)
n_profile_rows    <- nrow(.prof)
n_llm_bounded     <- sum(.prof$is_bounded_low_impact == TRUE,  na.rm = TRUE)
n_not_llm_bounded <- sum(.prof$is_bounded_low_impact == FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
n_tx_not_bounded  <- sum(.prof$candidate_category == "Transmission__upgrade" &
                         .prof$is_bounded_low_impact == FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**How we define a "CE-shaped" candidate.** A dedicated LLM pass reads each FONSI and assigns its
action type (`action_category`) and whether the action is inherently small/routine/low-impact —
classifying by what the action physically *is*, not by keywords in the title. A candidate is
CE-shaped when the model judges it low-impact and, for transmission, the work modifies an
*existing* line within an existing right-of-way (not a new greenfield build). That narrows the
`r n_candidate` candidate FONSIs to the `r n_ce_shaped` CE-shaped projects used throughout
this report. The rest are not dropped: the larger rebuilds (`r n_tx_not_bounded` transmission,
many far longer than a CE would allow), utility-scale builds, and new-corridor lines move to the *expand / develop* bucket
(the worked example), where a broadened or new CE — not adoption — would be the fit.
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-sorting
#| fig-cap: "Every decarbonization FONSI by action type; teal = the bounded, low-impact subset kept for matching, grey = broader projects set aside."
#| out-width: 94%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_action_distribution.png"))
```

The kept subset shares a consistent **low-impact fingerprint** — the traits that make
these FONSIs CE-shaped regardless of any stated acreage or length. Most sit on land that
has already been disturbed and run inside an existing right-of-way; smaller shares are
explicitly temporary or state that they add no new permanent road. In plain terms: *these
are not greenfield builds — they are modifications within existing corridors, on ground
that has already been developed, which is exactly the low-impact signature a CE is meant
to capture.*

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-keep-bounded
#| fig-cap: "Share of the bounded subset with each low-impact siting trait. *The 'no new permanent access road' bar counts only FONSIs that explicitly say so, and therefore under-counts."
#| out-width: 82%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_keep_bounded.png"))
```

One honest caveat on reading this chart: the "no new permanent access road" bar is a
*conservative* flag — it fires only when a FONSI explicitly states no new road, so its low
share reflects under-reporting (most FONSIs simply do not address roads), not that the
rest build major new access. The two dominant, well-evidenced traits are *previously
disturbed land* and *within an existing right-of-way*. (Beyond what the chart shows, the
enrichment also records whether each action *tiers* from a programmatic review and its
overall *bounded, low-impact* judgment — further signals behind the same conclusion.)

## Resolve each cell: match to the CE catalog, then apply the rule

Each cell is compared against all `r comma(n_ce)` existing federal CEs to find its **closest match**
(a 0–1 text-similarity score blending semantic meaning and word overlap — a *ranking aid*, not a
percent of matching text). That match then resolves the cell to a verdict by a three-question rule:

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-align: center
flowchart TD
  A["For each tech × action cell:<br/>is there a close matching CE?"] -->|no close match| D["DEVELOP<br/>no CE exists — write a new one"]
  A -->|close match| B{"Do our FONSIs exceed<br/>the CE's stated size bound?"}
  B -->|yes| E["EXPAND<br/>widen the existing CE"]
  B -->|no| C{"Held at a different agency<br/>than the ones doing these EAs?"}
  C -->|yes| AD["ADOPT<br/>that agency adopts the CE"]
  C -->|no| CV["already covered (drop)"]
```

The coverage map above is this rule applied to every cell. The match score is a *ranking aid,
not the verdict*: scores are uncalibrated, so read them comparatively. A cell scored against a random,
unrelated CE sits near the grey baseline (≤ ~0.20); the cells that resolve to adopt / expand sit
well above it, while the develop cells fall closest to it — no existing CE covers them. Every
verdict is a **candidate pending eCFR confirmation**, not a legal finding.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-ce-match
#| tbl-cap: "Closest existing categorical exclusion to each recurring tech × action cell (n ≥ 5 CE-shaped FONSIs), by text similarity — a ranking aid, pending eCFR verification."
verdicts |>
  filter(verdict != "contrast", n_profile_fonsi >= 5) |>
  arrange(desc(best_ce_match_score)) |>
  transmute(
    `Tech × action` = str_replace_all(candidate_label, "_", " "),
    Verdict = ifelse(verdict == "new", "develop", verdict),
    `Closest existing CE (held by)` = paste0(best_ce_structured_id, " (", best_ce_agency, ")"),
    Similarity = sprintf("%.2f", best_ce_match_score)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12), column_labels.font.weight = "bold")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-ce-match
#| fig-cap: "Best-match similarity to an existing CE, per candidate (dashed line = the soft 0.40 reference)."
#| out-width: 84%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_ce_match.png"))
```

## Rank the opportunities

With every cell resolved, the opportunities — the adopt, expand, and develop cells — are
ranked so you know which to pursue first. Each gets a transparent score (0–1) summing six
factors; the bar length is the priority and the colors show why:

- **Novelty** — a brand-new CE (develop) outranks expanding or adopting one.
- **Volume** — how many bounded FONSIs back it (more evidence ranks higher).
- **Agency/state spread** — how widely the action recurs (broader = more agencies benefit).
- **Has size limits** — whether we can state a numeric bound (easier to write the CE).
- **Low mitigation dependence** — less reliance on case-by-case mitigation (a cleaner CE).
- **Recurring action type** — a flat baseline every grid cell shares (it lifts all scores equally, so it does not change the order).

Because the default score weights novelty most, the **net-new (develop) candidates rank
highest** — *Solar — other*, *Other Clean — upgrade*, and *Wind — demonstration / pilot* (nuclear's
demonstration cell ranks lower down). *Transmission upgrade* — the highest-volume single cell (the
*expand* lever in the Findings below) — sits a few places behind them; it leads only when you weight
raw volume most (the next table).

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-classification
#| fig-cap: "Each candidate's rank score, broken into its six contributing factors (bar length = total priority). Only cells with ≥ 2 CE-shaped FONSIs are ranked — empty cells are excluded."
#| out-width: 92%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_classification.png"))
```

The weights are a judgment call, so here is the rank order under three plausible weightings.
The leader changes with the weighting — transmission upgrade tops the *volume-heavy* view,
while the novelty-driven develop cells lead the others — so read the ranking as a **band of
strong candidates**, not a precise order:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-rank-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Rank of the top opportunity cells (≥ 2 CE-shaped FONSIs) under three weightings (volume-heavy / mitigation-risk-heavy / verification-confidence-heavy). The leader changes with the weighting, so treat the top group as a band, not a precise ranking."
rc <- verdicts |> filter(verdict != "contrast", n_profile_fonsi >= 2) |>
  transmute(Cell = str_replace_all(candidate_label, "_", " "),
            rank_novelty, rank_volume, rank_diversity, rank_limits, rank_mitigation, rank_role)
.score <- function(w) with(rc, w[1]*rank_novelty + w[2]*rank_volume + w[3]*rank_diversity +
                             w[4]*rank_limits + w[5]*rank_mitigation + w[6]*rank_role)
tibble(Cell = rc$Cell,
       `Volume-heavy`        = rank(-.score(c(.10, .50, .15, .05, .05, .15)), ties.method = "min"),
       `Mitigation-risk`     = rank(-.score(c(.10, .15, .10, .05, .45, .15)), ties.method = "min"),
       `Verification-conf.`  = rank(-.score(c(.15, .15, .10, .25, .10, .25)), ties.method = "min")) |>
  arrange(`Volume-heavy`) |>
  slice_head(n = 12) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_align(align = "center", columns = -Cell) |> cols_align(align = "left", columns = Cell) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12), data_row.padding = px(5))
```

## Findings: three CE opportunities

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
**These are candidate matches, not coverage determinations.** Each pairing below is a
*text-similarity* match between a recurring FONSI action and an existing CE at another
agency — it flags where adoption is worth reviewing, not that the CE legally covers the
action. Every match is pending verification against the current eCFR / agency CE text;
treat the verdicts as a prioritized review list, not a legal conclusion.
:::

The grid's `r n_cells` cells resolve to `r n_adopt` adopt · `r n_expand` expand · `r n_new` develop,
plus `r n_covered` already covered. (Both expand cells are transmission; the second — transmission
new-build — has no CE-shaped FONSIs in this corpus, so the Expand finding below covers upgrades.)
The three opportunity types follow in priority order — each self-contained below: **what it is**,
**how much evidence backs it**, and **what to do**.

### Expand — transmission upgrades (the strongest opportunity)

**The single highest-volume opportunity:** `r n_tx_up` in-corridor transmission FONSIs across
`r verdicts$n_states[verdicts$candidate_category=="Transmission__upgrade"]` Western states match an
existing CE, but a subset of long rebuilds runs past its ~25-mile cap — so the move is to widen
that cap, not adopt the CE as-is.

**Why *expand*, not *adopt* — the size test.** The *expand* test asks whether a cell's bounded
FONSIs exceed the matched CE's stated size limit. Transmission upgrades are the `r n_expand` cells
that fire it: the in-corridor rebuilds run a ~28-mile median — some far longer — against a ~2-mile
typical CE limit (max 25 mi). Most *other* cells can't fire a numeric expand — their closest CE
bounds scope with *words* ("routine," "minor," "existing infrastructure"), not a number — but that
absence is not "no expand opportunity exists"; it just has to be verified against the CE text.
The size panels below make the split concrete: only line length (green) runs past the limits CEs
typically state; voltage and acreage (blue) sit within them, so a conventional CE limit would fit.

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-sizes
#| fig-cap: "Context from the **full** CE catalog: bounded transmission FONSIs vs all stated CE size limits (log scale, boxplot + cases). The miles panel is shaded where our FONSIs exceed the limits CEs typically state — the transmission *expand* case. Study-area outliers excluded."
#| out-width: 86%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_sizes.png"))
```

**In detail — how the transmission case splits into two candidate CEs.**

```{r}
#| echo: false
tx_sp <- facts |> filter(candidate_category == "Transmission__upgrade", is_profile_subtype) |>
  distinct(project_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(txt = tolower(paste(coalesce(quoted_span, ""), coalesce(action_definition, ""))),
         reb = str_detect(txt, "rebuild|reconstruct|(remov|replac|install|new)\\w*[^.]{0,40}(structure|pole|tower|h-frame|monopole)"))
n_tx_total <- nrow(tx_sp); n_tx_adopt <- sum(tx_sp$is_bounded); n_tx_exp <- sum(!tx_sp$is_bounded)
n_tx17 <- sum(tx_sp$is_bounded & !tx_sp$reb); n_tx19 <- sum(tx_sp$is_bounded & tx_sp$reb)
```

The strongest-evidenced case: `r n_tx_total` transmission-upgrade FONSIs for in-corridor
work, across BLM, the power-marketing administrations, NNSA, and others in
`r verdicts$n_states[verdicts$candidate_category=="Transmission__upgrade"]` Western
states. TVA **already categorically excludes this work under two exclusions**, by work type:

- **CE #17 — modify in place:** reconductoring, uprating, equipment swaps, limited pole
  replacement. No length limit.
- **CE #19 — rebuild:** replacing the line's structures within the existing right-of-way.
  Capped at 25 miles.

Of the `r n_tx_total`, the model judged `r n_tx_adopt` adopt-ready (small / in-corridor):
`r n_tx17` map to CE #17 (modify) and `r n_tx19` to CE #19 (rebuild ≤ 25 mi). The
other `r n_tx_exp` are large rebuilds (full structure replacement, well beyond CE #19's
25-mile cap) it flagged as *not* inherently low-impact — so they are the
*expand / develop* case (an expanded or new CE), not a clean adopt.

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-ce-split
#| fig-cap: "The transmission FONSIs split by the model's low-impact judgment: adopt-ready (CE #17 modify / #19 rebuild ≤25 mi) vs the large rebuilds that are too big for the existing CE (expand / develop). #17-vs-#19 inferred from the action text."
#| out-width: 88%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_ce_split.png"))
```

Both exclusions, verbatim (key phrases bolded):

> *CE #17 — modify.* **Routine modification, repair, and maintenance** of, and **minor
> upgrade** of and addition to, **existing transmission infrastructure** … transmission line
> **uprate, modification, reconductoring** … and **limited pole replacement**. *(New access
> roads outside the right-of-way are capped at 1 mile — a road limit, not a line limit.)*

> *CE #19 — rebuild.* The **rebuilding** of transmission lines within or contiguous to
> **existing rights-of-way** involving generally **no more than 25 miles** in length and no
> more than 125 acres of expansion of the existing right-of-way.

The table below lists sample FONSIs from different agencies, each with a verbatim excerpt
from the cited record showing the in-corridor reconductoring/rebuild work these CEs cover.
Each row names the source document (EA or FONSI) and page, and the project title links to
the full record in the document explorer.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-transmission-example
#| tbl-cap: "Sample bounded transmission-upgrade FONSIs with verbatim, source-verified excerpts (titles link to the document explorer)."
# Verified action quotes from the LLM enrichment (candidate_facts.quoted_span): each was
# checked verbatim against the cited EA/FONSI page. Titles deep-link to the explorer (?pid=).
EXPLORER <- "https://huggingface.co/spaces/kaseyzapatka/nepa-document-explorer"
scope_rx <- "(?i)(reconductor|rebuild|replace|upgrad|existing|within|right.of.way|in.place|conductor|structure|pole|maintenance)"
drop_rx  <- "(?i)(finding of no significant|revision sheet|table of contents|environmental assessment$)"
rel_rx   <- "reconductor|rebuild|replace|upgrad|existing|within|right-of-way|right of way|in place|maintenance|conductor|structure|pole"

# trim an excerpt to a clean boundary: cut over-long quotes at the last clause/word, and
# drop a dangling partial word (some source quotes themselves end mid-word) so it never
# reads as cut off; add an ellipsis only when text was actually dropped
clean_cut <- function(s, n = 520) {
  s <- str_squish(s)
  cut <- nchar(s) > n
  t <- if (cut) substr(s, 1, n) else s
  if (cut) {
    m <- str_locate_all(t, "•|\\. |; ")[[1]]
    pos <- if (nrow(m)) m[nrow(m), 1] else NA_integer_
    if (is.na(pos) || pos <= n * 0.5) {
      sp <- str_locate_all(t, " ")[[1]]
      pos <- if (nrow(sp)) sp[nrow(sp), 1] else NA_integer_
    }
    if (!is.na(pos)) t <- substr(t, 1, pos - 1)
  }
  t <- str_trim(t)
  ends_clean <- str_detect(t, "[.!?\"')]$")
  if (!ends_clean) t <- str_replace(t, "\\s+\\S{1,3}$", "")   # drop a dangling short partial word
  if (cut || !ends_clean) t <- paste0(str_trim(t), " …")
  t
}

ex <- facts |>
  filter(candidate_category == "Transmission__upgrade", is_bounded,
         citation_verified,                       # "source-verified" = only quote-verified rows (#11)
         !is.na(quoted_span), nchar(quoted_span) >= 70,
         str_detect(quoted_span, scope_rx), !str_detect(quoted_span, drop_rx)) |>
  distinct(project_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    Source = ifelse(str_detect(tolower(citation_document_role), "fonsi"), "FONSI", "EA"),
    agency_raw = str_squish(str_remove_all(lead_agency_harmonized, '[\\[\\]"]')),
    # name the specific power-marketing administration so the column isn't all "PMA"
    Agency = ifelse(str_detect(agency_raw, "Power Marketing"),
      case_when(str_detect(quoted_span, "(?i)bonneville|\\bBPA\\b") ~ "Bonneville Power Administration",
                str_detect(quoted_span, "(?i)\\bWestern\\b|WAPA")    ~ "Western Area Power Administration",
                str_detect(quoted_span, "(?i)southwestern")          ~ "Southwestern Power Administration",
                TRUE ~ "Power Marketing Administration"),
      agency_raw),
    dept = case_when(str_detect(agency_raw, "Land Management") ~ "blm",
                     str_detect(agency_raw, "Power Marketing") ~ "pma", TRUE ~ "other"),
    relevance = str_count(tolower(quoted_span), rel_rx),
    # #19 = rebuild / structure replacement (≤ 25 mi); #17 = reconductor / in-place upgrade
    ce_bucket = ifelse(str_detect(tolower(quoted_span),
                       "rebuild|reconstruct|new structure|structure replacement|replac\\w*.{0,30}(structure|pole|tower)"),
                       "Candidate CE #19 — rebuild (≤ 25 mi)", "Candidate CE #17 — reconductor / in-place upgrade"),
    # trim long quotes to the last clean bullet/sentence so nothing dangles mid-word,
    # then bold the modify-existing-infrastructure language
    Excerpt = paste0("“", vapply(quoted_span, clean_cut, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE), "”"),
    Excerpt = str_replace_all(Excerpt,
      "(?i)(reconductor\\w*|rebuild\\w*|replac\\w*|upgrad\\w*|remov\\w*|existing|within the existing right-of-way|right-of-way|same alignment|in place)",
      "**\\1**")
  ) |>
  filter(dept %in% c("blm", "pma")) |>
  # project_id tiebreakers make the selection identical on every render (reproducible)
  group_by(dept) |> arrange(desc(relevance), desc(nchar(quoted_span)), project_id) |> slice_head(n = 3) |> ungroup() |>
  arrange(ce_bucket, desc(relevance), project_id)   # #17 group first, then #19

ex |>
  mutate(`Project title` = glue("[{project_title}]({EXPLORER}?pid={project_id})")) |>
  transmute(ce_bucket, Agency, `Project title`,
            Source = paste0(Source, ", p. ", citation_page), Excerpt) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "ce_bucket") |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = c(`Project title`, Excerpt)) |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = everything()) |>
  tab_style(style = list(cell_fill(color = "#EAF0F8"), cell_text(weight = "bold", color = "#012169")),
            locations = cells_row_groups()) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(11), table.width = pct(100), data_row.padding = px(6)) |>
  cols_width(Agency ~ pct(16), `Project title` ~ pct(22), Source ~ pct(9), Excerpt ~ pct(53))
```

### Adopt — cross-agency matches (broad but thin)

**The broadest but thinnest opportunity:** `r n_adopt` cells resolve to *adopt* — a close CE exists
at *another* agency the doing-agency could adopt, and the 2023 FRA now permits exactly that. But most
are thin: only `r n_adopt_sub` have ≥ 2 CE-shaped FONSIs (the table below), and the rest rest on a
single FONSI or none. So treat adopt as a menu of matches to verify, not one dominant case — the
gap figure shows the evidence weight behind each (how many bounded FONSIs are run as full EAs when a
candidate-matched CE may already cover them, pending verification).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-adopt
#| tbl-cap: "Candidate adopt opportunities (adopt cells with ≥ 2 CE-shaped FONSIs): bounded actions with a close CE match at one agency but run as full EAs at others (matches pending eCFR verification)."
url_for <- function(id) {
  u <- ce_land$canonical_source_url[match(id, ce_land$structured_id)]
  ifelse(is.na(u) | u == "", id, glue("[{id}]({u})"))
}

verdicts |>
  filter(verdict == "adopt", n_profile_fonsi >= 2) |>
  arrange(desc(rank_score)) |>
  transmute(
    `Tech × action` = str_replace_all(candidate_label, "_", " "),
    `Low-impact FONSIs` = n_profile_fonsi,
    `Existing CE (held by)` = paste0(vapply(best_ce_structured_id, url_for, character(1)), " — ", best_ce_agency),
    `Agencies that could adopt it` = adopt_targets,
    States = n_states
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = `Existing CE (held by)`) |>
  tab_source_note(md(paste0(
    "**Thin-evidence flag:** most adopt cells rest on only 2–4 low-impact FONSIs — ",
    "treat them as illustrative opportunities to verify, not robust findings. Some high-count rows ",
    "are non-physical actions (e.g. land / right-of-way authorization); a peer CE exists to adopt, ",
    "but confirm it fits the action."))) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13), column_labels.font.weight = "bold")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-adoption-gap
#| fig-cap: "Per adopt candidate: bounded FONSIs run as full EAs, and the existing CE they could adopt."
#| out-width: 90%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_adoption_gap.png"))
```

### Develop — net-new gaps

**The genuinely new opportunity:** `r n_new` cells recur with no close existing CE — invisible
under the old hand-picked categories — and `r n_dev_codif` of them are codifiable, so the move is to
draft a new CE. Every develop cell sits below the 0.40 match line: the closest existing CE
isn't close enough to adopt.

The cross-cutting standout is **demonstration / pilot facilities**, a develop gap for wind (9),
nuclear (7), and other clean-energy (4) projects — one new CE could cover research / demonstration
across technologies. (For geothermal and biomass the same action already has a matchable CE, so it
resolves to *adopt* — the method discriminates.) The rest are more technology-specific: solar
interconnection, small new-builds. Non-codifiable actions — battery manufacturing, land permits —
are set aside; a CE codifies a *physical* action.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-develop
#| tbl-cap: "Candidate develop opportunities: recurring tech × action cells with no close existing CE (closest match below the 0.40 line). Non-codifiable cells (battery manufacturing, land authorization) excluded."
verdicts |>
  filter(verdict == "new", is_codifiable, n_profile_fonsi >= 2) |>
  arrange(desc(n_profile_fonsi)) |>
  transmute(
    `Tech × action` = str_replace_all(candidate_label, "_", " "),
    `CE-shaped FONSIs` = n_profile_fonsi,
    States = n_states,
    `Closest CE (similarity)` = sprintf("%.2f", best_ce_match_score)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_source_note(md(paste0(
    "All develop cells fall **below the 0.40 match line** — the closest existing CE isn't ",
    "close enough to adopt. Demonstration / pilot cells recur across wind, nuclear, and other ",
    "clean-energy projects."))) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(13), column_labels.font.weight = "bold")
```

## Timing & the FRA caveat

The 2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act (FRA, June 2023) gave agencies explicit authority
to adopt another agency's categorical exclusion — the exact move this analysis
recommends. So the age of these EAs matters. Using decision dates merged from the
D4 timeline, **all but one** of the dated bounded FONSIs were decided *before* the
FRA — these agencies ran full EAs without the adoption shortcut now available. (Dates
are known for ~⅔ of the bounded set; the rest are undated in the D4 output.)

**This makes the finding a historical one.** The corpus is almost entirely pre-FRA, so it
shows where full EAs were run before the adoption shortcut existed — it identifies
where adoption review is likely worthwhile, not that agencies are still running these
EAs today. So the recommendation is: *pre-FRA EAs indicate likely adoption opportunities,
pending a post-FRA refresh.* Before any client action, that refresh is required — check
current CE-adoption use, recent (post-June-3-2023) EA/FONSI recurrence, and any agency
implementation guidance since the FRA. Until then these are candidates to review, not a
claim about current agency behavior.

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-timeline
#| fig-cap: "The bounded FONSIs by decision year (D4 timeline), relative to the FRA's June 2023 CE-adoption authority."
#| out-width: 88%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_timeline.png"))
```

# Analysis 2 — Mitigated FONSIs

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Methodology

1. **Data —** the mitigated FONSIs: the subset whose "no significant impact" finding depends on committed mitigation rather than the action being inherently low-impact (`r n_mit_corpus` of `r n_clean`, `r percent(mit_share_cor, 1)`).
2. **Flag** each FONSI's mitigation dependence from the LLM read — *case-specific-dependent* (the finding rests on committed mitigation) vs *design-feature-only* (inherently bounded) vs *none*.
3. **Measure** the mitigated share and the resource areas where mitigation recurs, within each action type.
4. **Read for CE design —** a mitigation that recurs consistently across a class is a codifiable CE design criterion; an idiosyncratic one is a disqualifier.
:::

> **Mitigated FONSIs** imply that the project will have "no significant impact" if the
> applicant commits to some form of mitigation. This analysis systematically examines the
> language surrounding mitigated FONSIs to determine if there are patterns of actions that
> are routinely mitigated and if we can capture those recurring mitigations as a new CE.

**Mitigation dependence is a *risk screen*, not a disqualifier.** A mitigated FONSI does not
mean the action class is unsuitable for a CE. It means a defensible CE for that class would
need to encode the *recurring* avoidance/minimization measures as design criteria and
exclude cases that hinge on *project-specific* commitments. So a high mitigated share is
a flag to read the measures, not a veto.

## How "mitigated" was determined

**How this analysis works.** The model reads each FONSI once and pulls four things (whether the
finding depends on mitigation, what role that mitigation plays, the committed measures themselves,
and the agency's "significant if X" thresholds); we then test each for recurrence — a measure
or threshold that recurs across a class can become a CE design criterion, an idiosyncratic one
cannot:

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 9
flowchart LR
  A["451 FONSIs"] --> B["Claude reads each one:<br/>the finding + the<br/>committed conditions"]
  subgraph X["What Claude extracts"]
    direction TB
    C["Does the finding depend on<br/>mitigation — and what role<br/>does that mitigation play?"]
    D["The mitigation<br/>measures themselves"]
    E["The agency's<br/>'significant if X' thresholds"]
  end
  subgraph Y["Does it recur across projects?"]
    direction TB
    F["Most depend on<br/>case-specific mitigation"]
    G["Measures do NOT repeat<br/>→ can't codify"]
    H["Thresholds DO repeat<br/>→ the codifiable CE bounds"]
  end
  B --> C & D & E
  C --> F
  D --> G
  E --> H
  style X fill:transparent,stroke:#012169
  style Y fill:transparent,stroke:#012169
```

For every one of the 451 FONSIs the model read the finding and the committed conditions and
set three fields:

- **Is it mitigated?** — does the "no significant impact" finding *depend* on
  committed mitigation, or is the action inherently low-impact?
- **What role does the mitigation play?** — one of: none (inherently low-impact),
  design-feature-only (impacts avoided by the project's own bounded design),
  case-specific-dependent (the finding rests on committed, project-specific mitigation),
  permit/consultation condition (required by another regime, not the FONSI's basis),
  monitoring-only, or unclear.
- **What's the significance threshold?** — the agency's explicit *"would be significant if it
  exceeded X"* statements, captured verbatim. These are a CE's natural numeric bounds — and,
  unlike the project-specific mitigation measures, they recur across projects.

The supporting mitigation text is captured verbatim and 97%-quote-verified, and
each FONSI is tagged with the resource areas its mitigation addresses (biological,
water, cultural…) from a fixed vocabulary, so we can measure which recur.

## Is it mitigated?

The mitigated pattern is **corpus-wide**: `r n_mit_corpus` of `r n_clean`
(`r percent(mit_share_cor, 1)`) decarbonization FONSIs are mitigated, and
`r n_mit_noncand` of those fall *outside* the five Analysis-1 candidate
types — so this is not a candidate-only artifact. By action type (including the large
*Other* pool, which is 61% mitigated):

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-mitigated-share
#| fig-cap: "Mitigated-FONSI share by action type across all 451 FONSIs — not limited to the Analysis-1 candidates."
#| out-width: 86%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_mitigated_share.png"))
```

Across the whole corpus, then, the share reaching "no significant impact" only with committed
mitigation:

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-mitigated-overall
#| fig-cap: "How many of the decarbonization FONSIs reach 'no significant impact' only with committed mitigation."
#| out-width: 96%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_mitigated_overall.png"))
```

### Examples: the committed mitigation

So you can verify the read, here are the model's mitigation summaries for FONSIs tagged
case-specific-dependent. These are **LLM-extracted summaries, not verbatim quotes** — the
verbatim, quote-verified text lives in the boundary table below and in `evidence_cited`:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-mitigation-examples
#| tbl-cap: "Sample committed-mitigation summaries (LLM-extracted from the cited FONSI/EA — model summaries, not verbatim quotes; titles link to the document explorer)."
EXPLORER <- "https://huggingface.co/spaces/kaseyzapatka/nepa-document-explorer"
enr |>
  filter(is_mit, !is.na(mitigation_summary), nchar(mitigation_summary) > 80) |>
  arrange(desc(nchar(mitigation_summary)), project_id) |>
  distinct(project_title, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  mutate(
    summ = vapply(mitigation_summary, clean_cut, character(1), n = 800, USE.NAMES = FALSE),
    # bold the project-specific measures so they stand out as the case-by-case commitments
    summ = str_replace_all(summ,
      "(?i)(reseed\\w*|reveget\\w*|erosion[ a-z]{0,12}control|sediment control|stormwater|spill prevention\\w*|dust (control|suppression)|noise (control|barrier|abatement)|buffer\\w*|setback\\w*|raptor\\w*|nest\\w*|migratory bird\\w*|\\bSHPO\\b|tribal consultation|cultural[ a-z]{0,12}monitor\\w*|biological monitor\\w*|wildlife|wetland\\w*|seasonal[ a-z]{0,12}restriction\\w*|timing restriction\\w*|weed (control|management)|best management practices|special[- ]status species)",
      "**\\1**")
  ) |>
  transmute(
    `Project Title` = glue("[{str_squish(project_title)}]({EXPLORER}?pid={project_id})"),
    `Committed mitigation (LLM summary; project-specific measures in bold)` = summ
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = everything()) |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = everything()) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(11), data_row.padding = px(10)) |>
  cols_width(`Project Title` ~ px(180),
             `Committed mitigation (LLM summary; project-specific measures in bold)` ~ px(460))
```

## What role does the mitigation play?

Across the `r n_mit_corpus` mitigated FONSIs the model's `mitigation_dependence` label is
almost entirely case-specific-dependent, so to see *what kind* of commitment recurs we
read each FONSI's committed-mitigation text and tag the mechanisms it relies on (a FONSI
can use several). The mix is dominated by case-by-case mechanisms — consultation / permit
conditions, monitoring, and site-specific avoidance — not standard, transferable design features:

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-mitigation-roles
#| fig-cap: "The roles mitigation plays across the 310 mitigated FONSIs — the share whose committed mitigation includes each mechanism type (a FONSI can use several, so shares sum to more than 100%). Derived from the mitigation-summary text."
#| out-width: 88%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_mitigation_roles.png"))
```

### The dependence is overwhelmingly case-specific

Of the `r n_mit_corpus` mitigated FONSIs, `r n_mit_dep_case` are case-specific-dependent —
the finding rests on project-specific mitigation, not on the action being inherently low-impact.
"Overwhelmingly case-specific" is simply the tally: `r n_mit_dep_case` of `r n_mit_corpus`
land in `case_specific_dependent`. The contrast with the next section is the point — the
significance *thresholds* do recur across projects, which is what makes *them*, not the
measures, the codifiable part.

> **One honest caveat.** `is_mitigated_fonsi` and `mitigation_dependence` are
> *near-equivalent judgments*: the model almost always pairs "the finding depends on
> mitigation" with "that mitigation is project-specific." So this is **one consistent
> signal, not two independent confirmations.** The FONSIs it reads as inherently
> low-impact (design-feature-only or none) are exactly the ones it flags as *not*
> mitigated. The substantive finding stands: when a FONSI leans on mitigation, that
> mitigation is tailored to the project — not a standard, transferable design feature.

### The mitigation language is project-specific

The measures themselves are written per project — SHPO consultation here, raptor-nest
buffers there, site-specific erosion plans elsewhere. Breaking every mitigation summary into
2–3 word phrases and counting them, **no phrase recurs** across projects. A CE therefore
cannot copy any one project's measures. What *does* recur is the resource area the
mitigation protects — consistently biological, soils, water, and cultural — and those are
what a defensible CE would distill into standing design criteria.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-mitigation-pattern
#| tbl-cap: "Mitigated-FONSI counts and the recurring resource areas by candidate action type (sorted by FONSIs examined)."
mit |>
  left_join(verdicts |> select(candidate_category, candidate_label, verdict), by = "candidate_category") |>
  filter(verdict != "contrast") |>
  arrange(desc(n_focus)) |>
  transmute(
    Action = str_replace(candidate_label, " \\(.*\\)", ""),
    `FONSIs` = n_focus,
    `Mitigated` = n_mitigated_fonsi,
    `Recurring resource areas` = str_squish(top_mitigation_resource_areas)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = everything()) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12), data_row.padding = px(6)) |>
  cols_width(Action ~ px(190), `Recurring resource areas` ~ px(330))
```

## The agency's "significant if X" thresholds

Alongside mitigation, the enrichment captures the agency's explicit
**significance-threshold** statements — *"would be significant if it exceeded X," "an
EIS would be required unless Y."* Those sentences are a CE's natural numeric bounds.

### Boundary language: the verbatim statements

Each is a verbatim, span-verified quote; real examples:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-boundary-examples
#| tbl-cap: "Verbatim significance-threshold statements — the agencies' own 'would (not) be significant' counterfactuals (the argument bolded). These are a CE's natural bounds; titles link to the document explorer."
first_threshold <- function(j) {
  x <- tryCatch(fromJSON(j, simplifyVector = FALSE), error = function(e) list())
  # require an explicit significance COUNTERFACTUAL — not a bare impact statement or a mitigation measure
  cond_rx <- "(?i)would[^.]{0,55}significant|significant (if|unless|when|because|provided)|significantly (below|within|less)|would not[^.]{0,45}(adverse|significant|exceed)|(below|within)[^.]{0,35}(threshold|guideline|standard|criteri|limit)"
  drop_rx <- "(?i)defines? significan|is defined (by|under|as)|definition of|\\bCEQA\\b|context and intensity|40 ?CFR|\\b1508|table 4-1|impact significance thresholds resource|located greater than"
  cands <- character(0)
  for (t in x) {
    s <- if (is.null(t$statement)) "" else str_squish(t$statement)
    if (nchar(s) > 45 && grepl(cond_rx, s) && !grepl(drop_rx, s)) cands <- c(cands, s)
  }
  pref <- cands[grepl("(?i)would (not )?be (a |an )?(potential\\w* )?significant|significant if", cands)]
  if (length(pref)) pref[which.max(nchar(pref))] else if (length(cands)) cands[which.max(nchar(cands))] else ""
}
bold_sig <- function(s) str_replace_all(s,
  "(?i)(would (not )?be (a |an )?(potentially )?significant|significant if|significantly (below|within|less)|would not be expected to have any adverse[ a-z]*)",
  "**\\1**")
EXPLORER <- "https://huggingface.co/spaces/kaseyzapatka/nepa-document-explorer"
enr |>
  filter(!is.na(significance_thresholds), significance_thresholds != "[]") |>
  mutate(stmt = vapply(significance_thresholds, first_threshold, character(1))) |>
  filter(nchar(stmt) > 45) |>
  distinct(project_title, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(desc(str_detect(stmt, "(?i)would (not )?be (a |an )?(potential\\w* )?significant|significant if")),
          desc(nchar(stmt))) |>
  slice_head(n = 5) |>
  transmute(
    `Project Title` = glue("[{str_squish(project_title)}]({EXPLORER}?pid={project_id})"),
    `Significance-threshold statement (argument in bold)` =
       bold_sig(vapply(stmt, clean_cut, character(1), n = 560, USE.NAMES = FALSE))
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_markdown(columns = everything()) |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = everything()) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(11), data_row.padding = px(8)) |>
  cols_width(`Project Title` ~ px(170), `Significance-threshold statement (argument in bold)` ~ px(450))
```

These are candidate CE bounds straight from the agencies' own findings — the
thresholds a new or adopted CE would be written to stay within.

And here is the key contrast with the mitigation measures: **unlike the measures, these
threshold *conditions* recur** across projects — which is exactly what makes them codifiable.
The most-common phrases in the agencies' "would be significant if …" statements:

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-significance-thresholds
#| fig-cap: "Most-frequent phrases in the agencies' explicit significance-threshold statements across the mitigated FONSIs. Unlike the project-specific mitigation measures (which do not recur), these conditions repeat — the natural, codifiable CE bounds."
#| out-width: 90%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_significance_thresholds.png"))
```

# Analysis 3 — Review of existing federal Categorical Exclusions

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Methodology

1. **Data —** the existing federal CE catalog (the [CE Explorer export](https://ce.permitting.innovation.gov/) — `r comma(n_ce)` CEs across `r n_units` agency units, each linking to its eCFR source).
2. **Compare** every CE to every other by text similarity.
3. **Flag** near-duplicates that recur at more than one agency.
4. **Group** those into shared "action families."
5. **Read** each CE's stated numeric limits, where it has any → what is already covered and how routinely agencies share the same CE (the precedent for *adopt*).
:::

> This analysis reviews all `r comma(n_ce)` **existing federal Categorical Exclusions**
> across `r n_units` agency units for patterns and insights.

## The CE landscape, by department and agency

The concentration is stark — **four of the `r n_units_dept` departments hold half of all
`r comma(n_ce)` CEs**:

```{r}

#| out-width: 78%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_ce_waffle.png"))
```

Within those departments, the individual agencies (the four big departments in teal):


## Numeric bounds are rare — and scattered

The single biggest fact about the existing catalog: **only `r n_bounds` of
`r comma(n_ce)` CEs state an explicit numeric limit.** The other
~`r comma(n_ce - n_bounds)` bound the action *qualitatively*.

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-ce-numlimit
#| fig-cap: "Of all 2,105 CEs, only 86 carry an explicit numeric limit; the rest are bounded with words."
#| out-width: 96%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_ce_numlimit.png"))
```

And the few that *do* carry a number are themselves scattered — acres and miles
dominate, but **every CE picks a different value.** The single most common acreage limit
(10 acres) is used by only 14 of the 71, and the stated limits run all the way from
1 to 10,000 acres. There is no common threshold to *expand* against:

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-ce-bounds-lolli
#| fig-cap: "Every stated acre/mile limit among the 86 CEs that have one; stick height = how many CEs use exactly that value. The values sprawl across the log axis and none dominates."
#| out-width: 86%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_ce_bounds_lolli.png"))
```

So a *numeric* "expand the stated limit" argument has little precedent to lean on — the
transmission cells are the exception in Analysis 1 (they exceed CE #19's 25-mile cap); for the
other cells, qualitative coverage gaps stay unverified rather than numerically exceeded.

### What the non-numeric limits look like

Most CEs bound scope with **words, not numbers** — consistent in spirit but disjointed
in form, each agency phrasing it differently:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-nonnumeric
#| tbl-cap: "How existing CEs bound scope without numbers."
qual <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Type, ~pat,
  "Routine / minor",           "(?i)\\broutine\\b|\\bminor\\b",
  "Small-scale / limited",     "(?i)small[- ]scale|limited (to|in)|small (number|quantit)",
  "Temporary / short-term",    "(?i)temporary|short[- ]term",
  "Within existing footprint", "(?i)existing (right|footprint|facilit|structure|disturb|road)")
pick <- function(p) {
  d <- ce_land$ce_description[!is.na(ce_land$ce_description) & str_detect(ce_land$ce_description, p)]
  d <- d[nchar(d) >= 45 & nchar(d) <= 320]
  if (length(d)) str_squish(d[1]) else ""
}
qual |>
  mutate(Example = vapply(pat, pick, character(1))) |>
  filter(Example != "") |>
  transmute(`Limiter type` = Type, `Example CE language (verbatim)` = Example) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = everything()) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"), locations = cells_body(columns = `Limiter type`)) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(weight = "bold"), locations = cells_column_labels()) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(11), data_row.padding = px(6)) |>
  cols_width(`Limiter type` ~ px(150), `Example CE language (verbatim)` ~ px(440))
```

## How related are the CEs?

Each point below is one CE laid out by text similarity (t-SNE of the embeddings), colored by its
k-means family and labeled by the family's distinctive phrases. The CE text **does not split
into cleanly separated clusters** — the silhouette is low and flat across every *k* (see the
[k-selection figure](#fig-d6-ce-elbow) below), so the k = 8 families are a *readability* grouping
of the layout, not a natural optimum. Even so, recognizable families emerge — real property &
rights-of-way, data collection / geophysical survey, hazardous-materials storage & disposal, airport
layout plans, goods & services, and regulatory/guidance actions — and many recur across *different*
departments, which is the precedent for adopt.

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-ce-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Every CE laid out by text similarity (t-SNE), colored by k-means family and labeled by its distinctive phrases. Closer = more similar wording."
#| out-width: 92%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_ce_scatter.png"))
```

The eight families, the topic each represents, and their distinctive keywords:

|---|---|

| Geological surveys and site assessments | geological / geophysical surveys, site assessments, data collection |

| Rules, standards, and guidance | rules, safety standards, product certification, labeling |
| Routine maintenance and minor ground work | routine facility maintenance, groundskeeping, dredging |
| Hazmat and disposal | disposal of property / fixtures / structures, hazardous materials |
| Monitoring and rights-of-way | monitoring equipment, rights-of-way, resident relocations |
| Airport layout plans and monitoring equipment | FAA airport layout plans, equipment installation, surveillance |

: The eight CE families — topic and distinctive keywords. {#tbl-d6-ce-topics}

## Cross-agency duplication — the precedent for *adopt*

**The point:** the same low-impact action is frequently excluded by *several* agencies
under near-identical language. `r n_xdup` CEs have a near-twin at a different
agency, forming `r n_xclust` shared "action families." Adopting a peer's CE — the
exact move Analysis 1 recommends — is not unusual; it is how the landscape already works.
*This shows adoption is common in the CE corpus; it does not verify that the
shortlisted adopt matches actually cover the D6 actions — that remains the pending eCFR check.*

The chart below shows how the twin families distribute across departments — each bar is the
number of families shared by *exactly* that set of departments:

```{r}
#| label: fig-d6-ce-upset
#| fig-cap: "Cross-agency CE 'twin' families by the set of departments that share them (top 12 combinations). A filled dot marks each department in the combination — the adopt precedent, visualized."
#| out-width: 94%
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(FIGS, "fig_d6_ce_upset.png"))
```

Each row in the table below is one shared family (not a single example): the action, how many
agencies use a near-identical CE for it, and a few of those agencies.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-cluster
#| tbl-cap: "Action families already categorically excluded by two or more agencies."
clusters |>
  filter(n_agencies >= 2) |>
  arrange(desc(n_agencies), desc(n_ces)) |>
  slice_head(n = 6) |>
  transmute(
    `Shared action` = str_trunc(str_squish(representative_desc), 240),
    `Agencies sharing it` = n_agencies,
    `e.g.` = str_trunc(agencies, 60)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_align(align = "left", columns = everything()) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(12), data_row.padding = px(7)) |>
  cols_width(`Shared action` ~ px(360), `Agencies sharing it` ~ px(80), `e.g.` ~ px(200))
```

The largest shared families are mundane (procurement, personnel, routine maintenance) —
which *is* the point: when an action is genuinely low-impact, agencies **converge on a
shared CE**. The decarbonization actions in Analysis 1 are simply ones where that
convergence hasn't happened yet.

## Where net-new CEs come from

Net-new CEs are not empty here — the grid surfaces `r n_dev_codif` codifiable *develop*
cells: recurring technology × action combinations with no close existing CE. The
cross-cutting standout is **demonstration / pilot facilities**, which recur as a develop gap
for wind (9), nuclear (7), and other clean-energy (4) projects — the single strongest candidate
for a brand-new CE. (For geothermal and biomass, that same action already has a matchable CE, so
it resolves to *adopt* — the method discriminates.) These gaps were invisible under the old
hand-picked five categories, which by construction only held well-trodden actions that already
had a CE somewhere.

A further frontier sits *outside* the named action verbs: of the 451 gridded FONSIs, the
model could only label `r n_action_other` with the catch-all action "other" (funding,
studies, efficiency work, and the like). **This deliverable did not decompose that bucket** —
it is a residual of un-named actions, not an examined pool. More net-new CEs plausibly live
there, but confirming that requires the recommended next step: cluster those "other" FONSI
action descriptions to surface recurring categories no one has named yet.

# Caveats & next steps

- **LLM-extracted, verified facts.** Action definitions, numeric limits, mitigation
  dependence, and significance thresholds come from a one-pass enrichment of all
  451 decarbonization FONSIs (Claude Sonnet); every quoted value was checked verbatim
  against its cited source page (97% verified). Values that did not verify are
  flagged, not shown.
- **CE matches are a ranking aid, not verified coverage.** Confirm each candidate
  CE against its eCFR text before acting on it — this is the one remaining
  verification step. The [CE coverage verification worksheet](../notes/deliverable06/ce_verification.html)
  pairs each candidate with its best-match CE, a first-pass coverage read, and the
  exact bound to confirm.
- **Recommended next steps:** (1) verify the `r n_adopt` adopt matches against the
  eCFR CE text (start from the [verification worksheet](../notes/deliverable06/ce_verification.html));
  (2) cluster the `r n_action_other` *"other"*-action FONSIs to search for additional net-new CEs.

## Assumptions & sensitivity

The conclusions rest on a few explicit assumptions — here is how each would move the result:

- **Every FONSI is placed in the grid** by its technology (from D3) and its LLM-labeled
  action verb — no candidate category is hand-picked, so the scan is exhaustive over the
  451 FONSIs. The one residual is the `r n_action_other` FONSIs whose action the model could
  only label "other"; those cells exist in the grid but their internal structure is not
  decomposed here.
- **"CE-shaped" adds a transmission shape gate** on top of the LLM's `is_bounded_low_impact`
  judgment (transmission must be modify-existing within an existing ROW). Dropping that gate —
  the looser, LLM-bounded-only definition — would *raise* the set from `r n_ce_shaped` to
  `r n_llm_bounded`, mostly by admitting large within-ROW reconductors that exceed a CE's
  typical mileage cap.
- **A retrieval score ≥ 0.40 is treated as a close CE.** This threshold is what separates
  *adopt/expand* cells (a close CE exists) from *develop* cells (none does); the adopt/expand
  matches clear it comfortably, so they are insensitive to moving the cut to 0.50.
- **The expand test keys on numeric bounds.** Most matched CEs are qualitative, so no
  *numeric* expand fires for them — but transmission upgrades exceed CE #19's ~25-mile cap,
  so `r n_expand` cells resolve to expand. Qualitative coverage elsewhere remains unverified.
- **Ranks use fixed component weights.** They separate transmission (n = 26 bounded) from the
  thin-n candidates clearly; for n < 10 read priority bands, not exact ranks (a formal
  weight-sensitivity table is a recommended follow-up).
- **CE coverage is unverified.** Requiring verified eCFR coverage before "adopt" reclassifies
  all `r n_adopt` to *candidate-pending* until that review is done.

## Run manifest & data completeness

```{r}
#| label: tbl-d6-manifest
#| echo: false
.enrall <- read_parquet(file.path(ANALYSIS, "fonsi_enrichment.parquet"))
ver_rate <- mean(facts$citation_verified, na.rm = TRUE)
miss <- tibble(
  Field = c("`is_mitigated_fonsi`", "`is_bounded_low_impact`", "`decision_date` (D4)",
            "verified action quote", "`disturbance_acres`", "`line_miles`"),
  `Null / missing` = c(
    sum(is.na(.enrall$is_mitigated_fonsi)),
    sum(is.na(.enrall$is_bounded_low_impact)),
    sum(is.na(facts$decision_date)),
    sum(!facts$citation_verified),
    sum(is.na(facts$max_acres)),
    sum(is.na(facts$max_miles))),
  `Treated as` = c("unknown (not mitigated=FALSE)", "unknown (not bounded=FALSE)",
                   "undated (shown separately)", "flagged; excluded from 'source-verified' tables",
                   "no stated acreage", "no stated length"))
miss |> gt() |> fmt_markdown(columns = Field) |> cols_align("left", columns = everything()) |>
  tab_header(title = md(sprintf(
    "**Run:** Claude `claude-sonnet-4-6` · schema `d6_enrich_schema_v5` · %d/%d FONSIs enriched · quote-verification %.1f%% · 1 no-evidence row excluded",
    n_enriched, nrow(.enrall), 100 * ver_rate))) |>
  tab_options(table.font.size = px(11), data_row.padding = px(4))
```

Null booleans are read as unknown, never as `FALSE`; the no-evidence row is carried with a
status flag, not silently dropped.

# Reproduction

The report is **LLM-backed**: action facts, numeric limits, mitigation, and significance
thresholds all come from a one-pass enrichment of the FONSIs. That enrichment is a
prerequisite and is not regenerated by `_run.py`. From the repository root in the
`nepa` conda environment:

``` bash
# 1. LLM enrichment (REQUIRED first; billable Anthropic pass, --dry-run for cost only)
#    model claude-sonnet-4-6, schema d6_enrich_schema_v5, ~451/452 FONSIs ->
#    data/analysis/deliverable06/fonsi_enrichment.parquet
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable06/03_enrich_llm.py --workers 4

# 2. deterministic chain 01->08 (09 wires the enrichment into facts/verdicts)
conda run -n nepa python phase2/code/deliverable06/_run.py

# 3. render
quarto render phase2/reports/deliverable06.qmd
```

`_run.py` executes the numbered chain `01`→`08` (the `08_create_figures.R` figures step needs
`Rscript`). **Without step 1 it now aborts at `09_wire_enrichment.py`** — 08 and this report
read `fonsi_enrichment.parquet` unconditionally, so a deterministic build does not reproduce
the reported figures and claims. Outputs are written to:

-   `phase2/data/analysis/deliverable06/` — analysis parquets (verdicts, mitigation, CE landscape/clusters)
-   `phase2/output/deliverable06/` — `figures/`, the slim comparison table, and `review/` drill-down tables
